background: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this local crop from an existing gold Guan Yu illustration. Remove ONLY the lower ornamental dragon-shaped golden weapon head and its broad green metal blade, starting just beneath the last gold shaft cuff near crop coordinates (406,114), and continuing down-left to the left image edge near y560. Keep the short stack of gold handle collars at the upper-right above that cut point. Fill the removed blade's footprint with a seamless continuation of the EXISTING surrounding green energy ribbons and dusty broken-wood battlefield ground. Do not invent a new weapon, hand, horse part, armor or new objects. Preserve the horse/tail/armor near the upper and right borders and the ground elsewhere, no redesign. This will be used only as a tightly masked background-repair patch; the original weapon head itself will be moved without regeneration. Keep the crop's exact layout and perspective. Output the same 2:3 portrait aspect ratio at 1024x1536, corresponding exactly to this 512x768 input crop at two times scale, with no framing/camera/position change.
shaft: Use case: precise-object-edit / isolated material continuation. The reference is a close crop of an existing polished dark metal pole held by Guan Yu. Create only an isolated straight cylindrical continuation of that SAME steel pole, on a truly transparent background. It is a dark warm gunmetal/bronze-brown steel shaft with a slim silvery warm highlight along its length, NOT wood grain. Draw it perfectly horizontal, exactly straight, constant diameter, viewed broadside without perspective foreshortening. The main shaft should extend nearly across the full image width with parallel outer edges and smooth continuous metallic material. At the RIGHT end only, add a very small neat closed bronze-gold butt cap, the same width as the rod, not a flared collar. LEFT end is just the straight open-ended continuation surface with no decoration, for seamless joining. No blade, no hands, no background, no glow, no shadows on a ground plane, no extra ornaments. Long thin pole: length about 12 times the diameter. Keep generous transparent margin around the single object so it can be rotated and composited onto the existing painting. Preserve physically simple steel construction and match the old reference's material rather than changing its style.
